newsitem.title: USA: CSCE coffee ends up on weather-related buying.
newsitem.headline: CSCE coffee ends up on weather-related buying.

text.p: CSCE coffee futures ended higher in thin trading Monday as forecasts calling for cooler temperatures in top-grower Brazil sparked some commission house and local buying, traders said.
"The buying was weather-related," said one trader. "They are forecasting cooler weather over the weekend. "This is the critical time of the year -- the first two weeks of July especially."

Benchmark September arabicas rallied to a session high of 175.00 cents per lb before settling at 172.40 cents, up 3.10 cents on the day. September reached a low of 166.50 cents. Spot July finished 2.50 cents higher at 192.40 cents, while the outer months closed up 1.90 to 3.50.
The July/September switch narrowed to 20.00 cents from 20.60 cents at the close Friday, while September/December widened to 21.50 cents compared with 20.30 cents.

Monday, Brazilian meterologists Somar said a polar air mass may pass through Brazil's coffee-growing regions from the evening of July 5, representing the greatest threat of frost seen so far this year.
The air mass could lead to temperatures of around zero degrees Celsius (32 F) in north Parana and southwest Sao Paulo states on the nights of July 5 and 6, Somar said.

But U.S. forecaster Weather Services Corp said Monday that no damaging cold is indicated as a warm, high pressure dominating Brazil's coffee belt is expected to remain basically unchanged for the next seven days. Cold weather building in central Argentina later this week is expected to pass well south of the coffee belt, WSC added.
"The possibility of frost next Sunday is too far away and not likely to have much consequence," said Refco Inc. analyst Ann Prendergast. "I think the market is just looking to find it right level."
Technically, traders said the high of 175.00 cents for September would provide nearby resistance, followed by 181.00. Support was pegged at 165.00 cents, they said.
After Monday's close, CSCE reported certified coffee stocks rose by 2,224 60-kg bags as of June 27, to 45,893 bags. However, there were 12,130 bags pending grading, the exchange said.
Volume was exceedingly light at an estimated 3,389 lots.
